title: MiniMed targets competition with upcoming diabetes devices

summary: The cardiovascular unit grew by double digits in the company’s fiscal second quarter, supported by its cardiac ablation solutions portfolio.
title: Medtronic continues to see growth in cardiovascular business

summary: Heraeus Medical Components has asked customers to immediately cease use and distribution of certain vascular guidewires. The product removal, which the Food and Drug Administration communicated on Friday in an early alert, reflects an issue with the quality of the hydrophilic coating on some guidewires. As of Nov. 5, Heraeus had not received any reports of serious injuries or deaths linked to the issue, but the quality problem could result in the release of particles that could block blood vessels.
title: Heraeus pulls vascular guidewires over coating detachment risk

summary: Nick Alexos will join the orthopedics company later this month after holding CFO roles at Univar Solutions and Dentsply Sirona.
title: Smith + Nephew names new CFO

summary: Danaher said Friday it has partnered with Microsoft to develop an agentic artificial intelligence platform to support its instruments. The partners will create the platform using Microsoft’s Azure cloud infrastructure and Foundry system for building and governing AI agents. Danaher plans to start launching agent-enabled instruments this year, with software for its high-content cellular imaging systems among the first products on its roadmap.
title: Danaher partners with Microsoft to create an agentic AI platform

summary: Zimmer Biomet has filed for 510(k) clearance for an autonomous version of its Monogram orthopedic robot, a company spokesperson told MedTech Dive in an email. CEO Ivan Tornos said at an investor event this week that Zimmer made the filling on Monday and hopes to receive Food and Drug Administration clearance sometime next year. Tornos said he expects Monogram to be a “game-changing platform,” citing the robot’s safety, efficiency, ease of use and accuracy.
title: Zimmer submits Monogram robot to FDA

summary: Johnson & Johnson said Thursday the first hospital to commercially install and use its Ottava robotic surgery system will be Memorial Hermann-Texas Medical Center. Tim Schmid, J&J’s worldwide chairman for medtech, said in a statement that the milestone is a significant step toward the company’s ambition to lead in surgical robotics. The Houston-based hospital will be the first in the U.S. to use Ottava as part of J&J’s early access commercial program.
title: J&J to install first Ottava robot in US hospital

summary: Abbott said Thursday it has started the VOYAGER CE clinical trial of its investigational Encantor transcatheter aortic valve implantation system. The trial is evaluating the software-guided, balloon-expandable system in up to 300 symptomatic severe aortic stenosis patients in Europe and Australia. Abbott plans to start a pivotal trial in the U.S. in the coming months. Encantor’s balloon-expansion system differentiates it from Abbott’s Navitor TAVI system, which uses a self-expanding valve. Abbott sees the devices as complementary.
title: Abbott starts trial of Encantor transcatheter aortic valve

summary: Analysts hailed Cunningham’s experience as a boost to GeneDx as the company tries to enter new markets and maintain its leadership in a competitive sector.
title: GeneDx appoints Everett Cunningham as CEO

summary: Diabetes tech firms Senseonics and Beta Bionics launched an integration this week of their glucose sensors and insulin pumps. Senseonics makes a continuous glucose monitor that can be implanted for up to a year, called Eversense 365. That device is now compatible with Beta Bionics’ iLet Bionic Pancreas automated insulin delivery system. The integration follows a partnership that the two companies struck in September. In the future, they plan to also pair Senseonics’ one-year CGM with Beta Bionics’ new tubeless patch pump, called Mint.
title: Senseonics, Beta Bionics integrate diabetes technology
